doc.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023

chapter: Women in jazz and the business
title: Women in jazz and not being labelled 'female guitarist'
summary: Rowe contrasts 1964 and 2023 DownBeat; Bailey says only one list matters and she did not market gender until she became Berklee assistant chair.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Um hum. There’s two topics that are often subjects of scholarly writings. One is jazz and race, and the other one that I’d like to bring up is women in jazz. And I found this in my stuff here — this is an issue of DownBeat December 1964. And I was looking through it and the only mention of a woman musician was a letter writer to the editor saying, “Nancy Wilson is beautiful.” Apparently they did have her on a previous cover. And he wrote in to say that that’s the best cover ever. So that was 1964. Now if we fast forward to — this is the latest issue of DownBeat, the 2023 Critics’ Poll. And I’m not sure how I got into this but I counted how many categories in the Critics’ Poll and if you include what they call “rising stars” there’s like 60 categories and 25 of them the number one person is a woman.
Yeah. And have you ever had issues in the business?

Well if we were to say the business is a microcosm of the world — you know — and we’re in an interesting time just dissecting gender, right? Like what does it really mean? So to me it doesn’t really mean anything in terms of picking up the guitar and playing it every day. Having two X chromosomes really doesn’t mean anything. I mean it’s not, you know, the physicality of the instrument — there’s nothing that would, you know, that I would need massive amounts of testosterone to be able to play it physically. So anyway I never concentrated on it, and I’ve had plenty of opportunities where people wanted to push that aspect of my career and I would have to say only since I became the assistant chair at Berklee College of Music did it really dawn on me that I could be in a place of influence. But up until then actually I’ve made it not really a part of how I market my music. You know people will say, “You’re the best female guitarist.” I’m like there’s only one list. Either you can play or you can’t play. And if I’m not on that list, that’s the only list I’m shooting for. That’s the only list I ever wanted to be on. So that’s how I think about it.
Good point. I remember Marian McPartland saying a similar thing — like with her wonderful accent you know, pointing out that oh she’s the finest woman jazz pianist.

Right, right, right, right, right. Yeah I mean in this art form hopefully it is about the music. We want it to be about the music. And I always say if you blindfold somebody — I mean is it they’re the best black guitarist, the best Italian-American guitarist. Is that how

we’re listening to music? It’s the best male guitarist, it’s the best female. I mean come on. Like life is complicated enough. Let’s just listen and play the music. Either you can play or you can’t play. That’s what it comes down to for me.
